In the time before time, the world knew only endless twilight. Neither day nor night existed, and all creatures wandered in perpetual gray dimness.

High in the mountains lived Solara, a weaver whose fingers moved faster than thought itself. She grew weary of the colorless world and decided to create something new. From the silver mist of morning, she spun the first thread of light. From the golden dust of distant stars, she wove the second. From the warm breath of sleeping dragons, she twisted the third.

One night, Selene wept for her solitude. Her tears fell upward into the darkness, and where each tear touched the void, it burst into brilliant light. Amazed, she began to weave.

She spun her finest thread and cast it skyward, weaving patterns of light across the emptiness. Each constellation told a story: the Hunter chasing eternal prey, the Bear protecting her cubs, the Twins who refused to be separated even in death.

But Selene grew old, and her hands trembled. Fearing her tapestry would fade, she made a final sacrifice. She wove herself into the sky, becoming the moon that watches over her creation.

Now, each night, the moon traces its path across the heavens, inspecting the star-stories. And when clouds obscure her work, she weeps again—her tears falling as rain to nourish the earth below.

The ancients say that shooting stars are threads coming loose, and when you see one, Selene is reminding us that even the most beautiful things require constant care and sacrifice.
